INFORMATION
Food and drink move from the Stomach to the Intestine and then into your body reserves. All rates use real play time.
STOMACH
Consumed Liquid and Solid enter the Stomach first. They may wait briefly before Moving into the Intestine. A Moving rate shows how quickly that content is leaving the Stomach.
INTESTINE
Liquid and Solid wait briefly in the Intestine before absorption. Liquid raises Hydration. Solid raises Nutrition. Absorbing shows the current reserve gain per real minute.
ENERGY AND STAMINA
Nutrition supplies fuel for Energy recovery. Hydration affects recovery efficiency. Work spends Energy and your current Energy determines how quickly Stamina can recover.
DIGESTIVE HEALTH
Digestive Health affects digestion speed and gut resilience. Illness effects and supplements can modify these values.
EXAMPLE: CANNED FOOD

Eat canned food and its Solid content enters the Stomach. After the stomach hold it Moves into the Intestine. It then Waits briefly before Absorbing. Nutrition rises over time instead of instantly. Rest can then use Nutrition to rebuild Energy.

Welcome to REBIRTH. You improve skills by using them, not by spending points. Open Character > Progression to see what trains each skill.

Books help you learn. Recipe cards and manuals unlock things to make. You may still need the right skill, tools and materials.

Start with the REBIRTH Challenges. Your journal adds short tips as you make progress. Gold titles are unread. Click a picture to enlarge it; use the mouse wheel to zoom and drag to move it.
Eating is only the first stage

Food and drinks take time to reach your body. They go into your stomach first, then your intestine. Nutrition and Hydration rise as your body absorbs them.\n\nOpen Character > Metabolism to see what is still being digested. Check before eating or drinking more. A full stomach does not mean your body has already recovered.
Carry water for automatic sipping

Keep drinking water with you. Check Hydration before a long trip.\n\nAfter drinking, give your body time to absorb the water. Open Character > Metabolism to check what is still in your stomach and intestine.
Let water reach your body

Drink clean water and allow digestion to absorb it. Water in the stomach is still pending hydration. This lesson completes when water absorption actually occurs; repeatedly drinking is not required.

Hydration is the body reserve on the right of Metabolism. Stomach liquid is still on its way; intestinal liquid may be Waiting or Absorbing. Watch the stage labels rather than expecting the reserve to jump immediately after drinking.

A negative NET rate means use exceeds incoming absorption at that moment. Reduce exertion when necessary and allow processing time. Do not mistake an empty intake panel for proof that you have no liquid still in the intestine.
Digest a meal

Eat a suitable meal and allow it to digest. Nutrition is not delivered instantly. Watch pending food and stomach fullness; give the meal time before eating more. This lesson completes during real nutrient absorption.

Nutrition measures the usable body reserve; the stomach measures pending contents. After a meal, inspect both the stomach and intestinal solid lines. Transfer and absorption are separate steps, so the Nutrition number can lag behind eating.

Choose food compatible with your character's diet and check its description before consuming it. Give pending portions time to work. Plan meals before travel and strenuous work rather than treating food as an instant emergency refill. The example picture shows one moment in digestion; its quantities are not universal requirements.
Prepare food you can use

Cooking gives you more food choices. Open a cooking station and check the recipe's ingredients and requirements.\n\nEat when you need food, then allow time for digestion. A meal in your stomach has not yet become Nutrition.
Prepare a drink

Complete an eligible prepared-drink recipe. Inspect the projected practice gain before crafting. Food and drinks train different skills; merely moving a bottle does not prepare a drink.

Preparing a drink and drinking it are different activities. Eligible completed preparation trains Drink Preparation. Consumption puts liquid into digestion; absorption later supplies Hydration.

Check the recipe's requirements and projected gain before spending ingredients. Carry an appropriate filled supply and inspect the hydration slot before travelling. Check a drink's effects rather than assuming every drink has the same role as clean water.
Treat a real need

Open Character > Condition to check an injury or illness. Read a medical item's description to see what it treats.\n\nUse the matching treatment, then check your condition again. Treating a real problem gives Medicine practice. Using supplies when you do not need them does not.
Learning by doing

Skills improve through useful actions. For example, hitting an enemy with a spear trains Spears. Swinging at empty air does not. Other weapon skills work the same way.\n\nOpen Character > Progression and select a skill to see how to train it. Books build Theory; using the skill builds practice. Both matter.
Study a fundamentals book

Fundamentals books and field notes build Theory for a skill. Their audiobooks offer another way to study the same title. Printed and audio editions share progress; they do not give two separate rewards.\n\nTheory supports learning. Useful actions build practical skill. Study a subject you use, then put it to work. Check Character > Progression to see your progress.
Learn a new recipe or procedure

Recipe cards, schematics, patterns and manuals teach specific knowledge. Some unlock recipes; others teach procedures or support abilities. Knowledge is separate from practical skill and Theory.\n\nCheck the recipe or ability in Character > Progression. Learning its knowledge does not replace required skills, materials, tools or stations.
Find an audiobook player

Craft Walkman and Headphones from one of each component and equip it in Character > Walkman. Use an audiobook cassette from your inventory or hold it and use it to start studying. You can move and work while listening.

Keep the cassette with you and the player equipped. Removing either pauses listening. Printed and audio versions share study progress and rewards.

Listening builds Theory; useful actions train the practical skill.
Start a herb supply
Save seeds for planting. Check a crop's recipe and planting requirements before using them.\n\nGrow food you plan to cook. Keep some of your harvest for the next planting.
Maintain your equipment
Check the repair material shown on a damaged item. Keep some with you before leaving home.\n\nRepair useful equipment when it needs it. Check the item afterward to confirm the repair.

Follow food through digestion

Eat a suitable portion, then inspect the stomach and intestine displays. Material first leaves the stomach and only later becomes available nutrition or hydration. Observe real transfer; a full stomach is not the same as a fully nourished body.
Recover Energy before another trip

After useful exertion, stop somewhere safe and let Energy recover. Check hydration and available nutrition: both support recovery. Stamina is the short-term exertion reserve; Energy supports it over a longer trip. This lesson requires an actual Energy increase.
Provide your own field meal
Prepare an eligible meal and digest food. Read diet compatibility, stomach volume and pending nutrition before eating. Do not keep eating simply because the current food meter has not risen yet.
Maintain a drinking routine
Prepare a drink and use the hydration slot. Inspect the remaining liquid before leaving, and confirm water is being absorbed. Carrying an empty bottle is not a drinking plan.
Keep working tools in service

Mine useful material, then earn Maintenance practice through a real repair or eligible maintenance work. Inspect repair requirements before a tool breaks. Different tools can require different supplies.
Recover and reuse components

Salvage useful parts and complete eligible Electrical work. Electrical components are distributed through appropriate technical loot; find the required service knowledge and supplies instead of repeatedly placing and removing a device.
Connect harvest to the kitchen

Harvest a mature crop and prepare food. Find plantable seeds in kitchens and food-store loot, then inspect the crop requirements. Planting and waiting are preparation; mature harvesting supplies the kitchen and trains Farming.
Use the whole hunting trip

Process an animal carcass and prepare food. The kill trains the weapon family; recovering meat and other materials trains Animal Processing. Cook with the recovered supplies and allow time for digestion.
Trade surplus for a useful supply
Make a meaningful sale and a different useful purchase. Sales train Trading and purchases train Bartering. Tiny repeated exchanges and selling back the same purchase are not a practice loop.
Plan for equipment burden

Travel with armor that adds a real burden and earn Athletics practice. Watch stamina while moving on a slope. Leave enough reserve to escape, then recover in safety rather than exhausting yourself beside an enemy.

Carry more with backpacks and toolbelts

Open Character. Under Survivor Gear, put a backpack in the Backpack slot or a toolbelt in the Belt slot. Shift-click the item in your inventory to equip it, or drag it into the matching slot. You can also select the item and choose Equip.

A Daypack adds 13 backpack slots. Each better backpack adds another row of 13. Your 26 encumbrance slots stay the same. A Utility Toolbelt adds two toolbelt slots; better belts add more.
